purpose: Defines `callisto status`'s cascaded-severity display and its folding of `validate`'s well-formedness checks into `status --check`'s exit-code contract, and `callisto add`'s interactive/non-interactive contract, replacing the standalone `validate` command consumers currently call.
scope: `status`'s per-package severity display for cascaded (dependency-driven) bumps; `status --check`'s exit codes and the diagnostic set it must cover after absorbing `validate`; removal of the `validate` command; migration of `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension_pdk.rs`'s `"validate"` dispatch arm and of `.github/actions/callisto-validate` to call `callisto status --check` and `callisto release --dry-run`; and `add`'s TTY-based interactive/non-interactive selection. Depends on SPEC-DX-RELEASE-COMMAND for `release --dry-run`'s existence (referenced by the callisto-validate action migration) and SPEC-DX-CLI-SURFACE for `validate`'s absence from `--help`.
non_goals: The 8-command `--help` inventory and jargon ban -- SPEC-DX-CLI-SURFACE.
`.github/actions/callisto-validate`'s and callisto-action's own workflow YAML wiring beyond the CLI commands they invoke.
Dependency-graph crosscheck diagnostics status already emits independent of this spec.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: For every package, `callisto status` shows the pending severity equal to `plan_version`'s `PlannedBump.severity` for that package (crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs), from the same computation `callisto version` uses, including cascade and fixed/linked-group bumps. Format: `<name> <version> (pending: <severity>)`, e.g. `b 1.0.0 (pending: patch)`. A package with no planned bump shows `none`; status computes no cascade of its own.
`callisto validate` is removed: invoking it fails to parse (clap 'unrecognized subcommand' or equivalent), not merely absent from `--help`.

`callisto status --check` covers every diagnostic `validate` (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs) currently reports that `status` does not already report on its own: `EmptyChangeset`, `EmptySummary`, `UnknownPackage`, `AmbiguousPackageName`, and `InvalidPackageName`. No diagnostic `validate` reported is lost by its removal.

`callisto status --check` is a conventional errors-only gate: exits 0 when the workspace has no error-level diagnostics (including the AC-03 set), regardless of pending changesets; exits 1 when one or more error-level diagnostics exist, regardless of pending changesets. `--strict` promoting a warning to error-level shifts the exit code from 0 to 1 accordingly (`--strict-graph` was removed in f3b1c1bcf along with the moon cross-check it escalated). Plain `status` (no `--check`) always exits 0 unless the command itself fails (e.g. workspace load or I/O error) -- it never gates on diagnostic severity. Pending state does not affect either exit code; it is read from `StatusReport`'s `pending` field (count of packages with a planned bump) in `--format json`, and from a summary line in text output.

[SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24: callisto-moon and the wasm32-wasip1 asset were removed; moon uses the CLI via proto] `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension_pdk.rs`'s `"validate"` dispatch arm (currently calling `callisto_graph::commands::validate::validate`) is removed or repointed at `status`'s check path; no dispatch arm in that file calls the removed `validate::validate`.

`.github/actions/callisto-validate` invokes `callisto status --check` and `callisto release --dry-run` in place of any removed command; it does not invoke `callisto validate`, `callisto publish`, `callisto plan-publish`, `callisto tag`, or `callisto filter-plan`.

`callisto add` with no `--package` flags, run with stdin attached to a TTY (per `tty::is_interactive()`, crates/callisto-cli/src/tty.rs, which tests stdin only via `IsTerminal`), enters the interactive wizard regardless of whether stdout is redirected.

`callisto add --package name:severity --summary <text>` (one or more `--package`, repeatable; `--summary` required) records the changeset without prompting, whether or not stdin/stdout is a TTY. Without `--summary` the flags path is rejected: "--summary is required when specifying packages via CLI flags in non-interactive mode" (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/add.rs:168-171).

`callisto add` with no `--package` flags and stdin not a TTY (e.g. piped) exits non-zero with an error naming the flags needed to proceed non-interactively, rather than hanging or printing a generic parse error.

reasoning: Grounded against origin/fix/release-run-simplify (HEAD 9be31095): crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:16-23 gives CascadeDecision's real fields (severity: Severity, not the revisions doc's informal 'PlannedBump.severity'), and cascade_action at line 25 is the function that computes it -- AC-01 cites the grounded names. crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs enumerates exactly five DiagnosticCode variants it emits (EmptyChangeset, EmptySummary, UnknownPackage, AmbiguousPackageName, InvalidPackageName); a grep of crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs found zero DiagnosticCode::-emitting call sites, confirming status does not already cover any of the five -- AC-03's set is exhaustive against validate's real diagnostics, not approximated. crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs confirms `validate` is still a live Command variant today (AC-02 describes pending removal, not already-shipped). crates/callisto-cli/src/tty.rs's doc comment and body confirm is_interactive() tests std::io::stdin().is_terminal() only, never stdout -- correcting a stdin-and-stdout misreading, grounding AC-07. crates/callisto-moon/src/extension_pdk.rs:66-72 gives the exact 'validate' dispatch arm AC-05 requires migrated. AC-04's errors-only 0/1 exit-code scheme and AC-06's callisto-validate action migration are the owner's stated defaults -- an earlier draft of AC-04 specified a four-way 0/1/2/3 scheme conflating error state with pending state; the owner corrected it post-implementation to a conventional 0/1 gate (pending state moved to `StatusReport.pending` instead), which this revision records. No `.github/actions/callisto-validate` directory exists in the workspace yet, so AC-06 specifies target behavior for an action to be created or updated, not a verified current wiring.
